purpose: Test whether lightweight local feature correspondence improves rotation beyond the preserved calibrated-gyro diagnostic
reference: calibrated-gyro v4; this experiment does not revise v4 strict selection

architecture.translation: freeze the entire existing MotionNet; keep its translation output
architecture.rotation: replace old residual with a zero-initialized correction about the actual causal calibrated gyro prior
architecture.shared_encoder: 1->8 k3s2p1 ReLU, 8->16 k3s2p1 ReLU; 12x16 feature grid
architecture.correlation: channel-normalized dot product at 9 offsets in a radius-1 local window; zero support outside image
architecture.spatial_pool: 3x4 average pool preserves a 4x4 grid per offset
architecture.head: 144 correlation features + 3 actual rotation prior values scaled by 0.01 + 5 normalized intrinsics/dt; Linear152->32 ReLU Linear32->3
variants: single-frame: current/current correlation with identical trainable parameters and schedule

training.optimizer: Adam on new rotation branch only
training.objective: SmoothL1 of calibrated rotation residual vector divided by fixed 0.01 radians
training.data: original 2388 train pairs from scenes2/3/4; 796 validation pairs from scenes5/6; no synthetic auxiliary/public training
training.checkpoint: lowest equal-episode accumulated validation rotation RMSE among epochs1..40; earlier on ties; retain this best trained candidate even if not eligible

acceptance.note: New v5 engineering budget permits at most 1% position degradation; not a reinterpretation of v4's stricter result. Otherwise retain reference. Both trained validation-selected candidates still receive public diagnostics.

timing: serial WASM runs after training and probes stop; wall time and deterministic fuel separately
budget: two 40-epoch CPU fits, no hyperparameter search, no paid compute
